extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners responding to 37 CFR 1.105 requirements)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from MPEP §§704–706 governing requirements for information under 37 CFR 1.105, examiner obligations after applicant replies, Patentability Reports, and standards for rejection of claims (novelty, obviousness, enablement, description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Art Relied Upon for Drafting Claimed Subject Matter (Form Para 7.117)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the title, citation and copy of each publication that was relied on to draft the claimed subject matter and a concise explanation of the reliance placed on that publication in distinguishing the claimed subject matter from the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are expressed as means or steps plus function, provide specific page and line numbers within the disclosure describing the claimed structure and acts. In bracket 1, insert a description of the most important inventive elements. Examiner Note: must be preceded by form paragraph 7.105 and followed by form paragraphs 7.122–7.126 as appropriate. Only documents actually relied on (not merely believed relevant) are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of Prior Art Search (Form Para 7.118)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether any search of prior art was performed; if a search was performed, state the citation for each prior art collection searched; if art retrieved was considered material to demonstrating the knowledge of a person having ordinary skill in the art, provide the citation for each such piece of art and a copy of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: must be preceded by form paragraph 7.105 and followed by form paragraphs 7.122–7.126 as appropriate. In bracket 1, describe the subject matter for which art is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names of Products or Services Incorporating Claimed Invention (Form Para 7.119)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the names of any products or services that have incorporated the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names of Products or Services Incorporating Disclosed Prior Art (Form Para 7.120)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the names of any products or services that have incorporated the disclosed prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate. In bracket 1, specify the attributes of the prior art that most closely approximate the claimed subject matter to narrow the focus of the reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details of Improvement Over the Prior Art (Form Para 7.121)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the specific improvements of the subject matter in claims [1] over the disclosed prior art and indicate the specific elements in the claimed subject matter that provide those improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph should appear at the end of the requirement for information, as appropriate. Preceded by and followed by form paragraphs as noted in Examiner Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Only Pertinent Pages Where Document is Large (Form Para 7.122)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the document is a bound text or a single article over 50 pages, the requirement may be met by providing copies of those pages that provide the particular subject matter indicated, or where such subject matter is not indicated, the subject matter found in applicant’s disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where the scope of information specifically includes copies of publications. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.105 and followed by form paragraphs 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of Fee and Statement Requirements for Certain Information Disclosures (Form Para 7.123)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee and certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 are waived for documents submitted in reply to this requirement when included in the applicant’s first complete communication responding to the requirement, but only for documents within the scope of the 37 CFR 1.105 requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any supplemental replies after the first communication and any information disclosures beyond the scope of the 1.105 requirement are subject to 37 CFR 1.97 fee and certification requirements. Examiner Note: use where scope includes citations to and/or copies of publications; must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.124 and 7.125 or 7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Good Faith Reply (Form Para 7.124)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply to the requirement must be made with candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56; where the applicant does not have or cannot readily obtain an item of required information, a statement that the item is unknown or cannot be readily obtained may be accepted as a complete reply for that item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: must be preceded by form paragraph 7.105 and followed by form paragraph 7.125 or 7.126 as appropriate. Should appear in the conclusion of any requirement for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion of Requirement That Accompanies Office Action (Form Para 7.125)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply to the enclosed Office action must include a complete reply to this requirement; the time period for reply to the requirement coincides with the time period for reply to the enclosed Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and appear at conclusion of any requirement that accompanies an Office action. If requirement mailed without other Office action, use form paragraph 7.126 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion of Requirement Mailed Without Any Other Office Action (Form Para 7.126)
rubrics_metrics.description: This requirement is subject to 37 CFR 1.134, 1.135 and 1.136 and has a shortened statutory period of [1] months; extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a) but reply cannot be extended beyond the maximum six months set by statute (35 U.S.C. 133).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and appear at the conclusion of any requirement mailed without any other Office action. The period for reply is ordinarily set for TWO (2) MONTHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion of Office Action That Includes Requirement (Form Para 7.127)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an Office action has an attached requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, a complete reply to the Office action must include a complete reply to the attached requirement; the time period for reply to the attached requirement coincides with the time period for reply to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph should appear at the end of any Office action that includes an attached requirement for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s Obligation Following Applicant’s Reply (MPEP §704.14(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must consider the information submitted with the applicant’s reply and apply the information as the examiner deems appropriate; identification of areas of search must be considered and indicated which areas were used and which not used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record search areas in 'Search Notes' form (see MPEP §719.05). If applicant provides written list of citations for submitted art, examiner must indicate which art has been considered and which not, similar to IDS under 37 CFR 1.97/1.98; may stamp list 'All References Considered' and include receipt date, application number and art unit. If applicant provides no list, no requirement for examiner to prepare one or make art of record unless examiner relies on such art in a rejection. It is never appropriate to refuse to consider information submitted in reply to, and within the scope of, a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement. Information beyond the scope need not be considered unless submitted in conformity with 37 CFR 1.97/1.98 and MPEP §609.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to Requirements Under 37 CFR 1.105 (MPEP §704.14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking withdrawal/modification of a 1.105 requirement or to have information considered may submit a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to the Director of the Technology Center; but a petition is not a reply and the time to reply continues to run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where information is submitted in reply to a 1.105 requirement, the examiner may NOT make the next Office action relying on that art final unless all instances of application of such art are necessitated by amendment. This practice differs from submissions under 37 CFR 1.97/1.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability Report (P.R.) Referral Standard (MPEP §705)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application contains one or more claims classifiable in other Technology Centers (TCs) which are not divisible inter se from claims governing classification, the application may, in extraordinary circumstances, be referred to other TC(s) for a Patentability Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.R. is a memorandum including citations of all pertinent references and a complete action on all claims involved; field of search must be recorded in 'Search Notes' (MPEP §719.05). Use only when it will save total examiner time or improve quality due to specialized knowledge. Not proper where claims are related in ways such that one examiner can adequately examine all claims (examples provided). Forwarding TC should not treat forwarding as a transfer; counting/recording rules apply. If disagreement as to classification or report results, procedures exist (consulting, panels, removal of report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewer Assistance for P.R. Cases (MPEP §705.01(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: In situations where an interview is held on an application for which a Patentability Report has been adopted, the reporting Technology Center may be called on for assistance at the interview concerning claims treated by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§713–713.10 regarding interviews in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal and Timing for Rejection Articulation (MPEP §706 intro)
rubrics_metrics.description: After understanding the claimed invention and performing a prior art search, the examiner should determine whether claims define a useful, novel, nonobvious, and enabled invention that is clearly described, and clearly articulate any rejection early in prosecution so applicant can reply and provide evidence of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where information reasonably necessary for examination should be required under 37 CFR 1.105, such requirement should generally be made either prior to or with the first Office action on the merits and should follow MPEP §704.10 et seq. Examiner should not overlook role in allowing claims which properly define the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection Content and Best References (37 CFR 1.104 / MPEP §706(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If invention is not patentable, claims (or unpatentable claims) will be rejected. In rejecting claims for lack of novelty or obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command, designate the particular part relied on when reference is complex, clearly explain pertinence, and specify each rejected claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may rely on admissions by applicant or facts within his/her knowledge. Includes rules on treating subject matter as commonly owned for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) and 103(c) (statements to that effect, joint research agreements, disclosure of parties). See moved sections for detailed guidance (MPEP §§2120, 2132–2156, 2142, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform Application of Patentability Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of patentability (patent eligible, useful, novel, nonobvious, enabled, and clearly described under 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112) must be the same throughout the Office; 'picture' claims are not alone justification for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application should not be allowed unless issues pertinent to patentability have been raised and resolved in examination and prosecution. The standard applied is 'preponderance of the evidence' — reject if, in view of prior art and record evidence, it is more likely than not the claim is unpatentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Claims Otherwise Allowable But Defective in Form (MPEP §706.01 II)
rubrics_metrics.description: When patentable subject matter is disclosed and claims are intended to be directed to such subject matter but cannot be allowed due to defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection or rejection but should be constructive and offer a definite suggestion for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: dependency on a rejected claim where dependent claim is otherwise allowable (see MPEP §608.01(n)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable Subject Matter Disclosed but Not Claimed (MPEP §706.01 III)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner is satisfied that patentable subject matter has been disclosed and the record indicates applicant intends to claim it, the examiner may note in the Office action that certain aspects/features have not been claimed and that properly claimed such claims may be favorably considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a constructive practice to inform applicant of potentially allowable claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction Between Rejection and Objection; Review Pathways (MPEP §706.01 IV/V and Contrasts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal to grant claims for unpatentability is a 'rejection' (subject to PTAB review). Matters of form are 'objections' (practical difference: rejections subject to PTAB review; objections only via petition to the Director). Formal matters should not be combined in appeals to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will not hear issues pertaining to objections/formal matters not properly before it; avoid combining formal matters in appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection on Prior Art — Language and Frequency (MPEP §706.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most frequent ground of rejection is unpatentability in view of the prior art (lack of novelty under 35 U.S.C. 102 or obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103). Language used in rejecting claims should be unequivocal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For detailed guidance on choosing best art, reliance on abstracts/foreign language documents, distinction between 102 and 103, and related material see the referenced MPEP sections (e.g., §§2120, 2132–2156).
